claim: Maxwell's analogy work was a staged construction of hybrid models: pick a source domain, narrow it with target constraints, then abstract generically to a model class.
agent_test: Compare agent that must state constraints from target and prune source vs. free analogy, equal tokens, on novel-mechanism tasks.

claim: Real expert analogies are mostly structural with no surface overlap (about 78% in the economics group; over half in biology labs and politics). Distance is NOT even: it depends on setting. Microbiology labs 98% within domain (Dunbar), psychology labs over 75% (Saner and Schunn), engineering design 55% within and 45% outside, political writing for the public 77% outside.
agent_test: Test retrieval by structure vs surface keywords at equal tokens; set source distance by audience and goal, not a fixed far default.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Analogy does conceptual work via four steps: highlighting, projection of candidate inferences, re-representation, and use of alignable differences (Kepler case).
agent_test: Prompt with explicit align, project, re-represent, check-differences steps vs. plain analogical prompting.

claim: Model-based reasoning (analogical, visual, simulative) is how scientists generate new concepts; this rests on case studies and ethnography, argued by bootstrapping not statistics.
agent_test: Not directly testable; use as design rationale. Compare an explicit model-building operator vs none.

claim: GPT-3-class models beat undergraduates on text matrix and letter-string analogies in the standard form, but trail on far story analogies.
agent_test: Re-run on current model with standard and far items; only one lab produced the human baselines.

claim: The Webb result does not generalise to counterfactual letter-string tasks: humans 0.753 accuracy vs GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452; Stevenson finds the same drop on symbol alphabets for all LLMs (GPT-4o 0.85 to 0.48) while adults hold at 0.88 to 0.89.
agent_test: Test the agent on permuted-alphabet and symbol analogies; report drop from canonical form.

claim: The permuted-alphabet failure looks like a counting bottleneck, not an analogy failure: in the published version GPT-4 with code execution matches humans (P=0.92); with code disabled it falls back to GPT-4 level (22.5% vs 21.7%, P=0.73); chain of thought does not close the gap (P=3e-8 vs humans). The preprint figure P=0.496 is superseded.
agent_test: Same model with code tool on and off, plus a modern reasoning model; no 2025 reasoning model has been tested on the permuted letter-string task.

claim: Models fail ARN when a far analogy competes with a surface-similar distractor: 29.1% for GPT-4 and 33.9% on average over 9 systems (random 50%, humans 91.4%). The 39.6% headline is the mean of the two far-analogy cells (45.3 and 33.9) across all 9 systems, not a single-model far-analogy score. GPT-4 on far-vs-far is 57.1.
agent_test: Test a structure-first step (extract each story's abstract message, then compare) on the far-analogy vs near-distractor cell with a 2025 reasoning model.

claim: Self-generated analogical exemplars give small gains over 0-shot and few-shot CoT (GSM8K 77.8 vs 75.8 to 76.7; MATH 37.3 vs 33.9 to 34.9) and need a capable model; self-consistency adds more (85.3).
agent_test: Re-test on the current model with equal token budget against plain self-consistency.

claim: Simulation tools help when the state is hard to track: a physics engine gave +27.9 points zero-shot (Mind's Eye) and text grids helped on spatial tasks. A control where a rule shortcut exists (ring navigation, modular arithmetic) showed no gain (CoT 52.5 vs VoT 49.5, n=200, not significant). Token break-even was not measured by anyone.
agent_test: Add a simulate step and log tokens; compare on tasks with and without a rule shortcut.

claim: LLM ideas are rated more novel than expert ideas (4.84 human vs 5.64 AI) but less feasible, with heavy duplication (about 200 unique of 4,000) and weak self-judging.
agent_test: Novelty vs feasibility blind review of agent output; add dedup and feasibility check.

claim: Retrieved far inspirations raise novelty only modestly and generated ideas still fall short of real papers (SciMON 85% ground truth better; MOOSE novelty 2.957 random vs 3.364 BM25).
agent_test: Compare random vs relevance-targeted inspiration retrieval at equal tokens.

claim: Law-discovery agents struggle as systems get complex, not equations harder: GPT-5 87.5 vanilla hard vs 40.3 complex hard; non-thinking models under 10%.
agent_test: Test the agent on multi-part systems with hidden interactions.

claim: A code interpreter helps weak models (GPT-4.1 5.8 to 18.9, +13.1) and slightly hurts most strong ones (GPT-5 75.9 to 73.3, -2.6; Gemini-2.5-flash -9.7; DeepSeek-R1 -6.0). Gemini-2.5-pro gains on the hardest cell (16.7 to 22.2). ConceptARC shows the same direction in text (o3 77.1 to 75.6, Claude 60.2 to 55.0, Gemini 66.0 to 60.4). The explanation (less exploration) is only correlational.
agent_test: Offer the tool but test an exploration quota; no one has run it.

claim: Benchmarks built on known equations may mostly measure memory: best symbolic accuracy only about 28 to 32% on shifted problems (LLM-SRBench).
agent_test: Use shifted or counterfactual versions for any discovery test.

claim: Non-LLM systems rediscover laws from data (AI Feynman 100 of 100 equations, AI-Newton), so rediscovery alone does not show LLM-style model-based reasoning.
agent_test: Use as baseline and as a tool the agent may call.

claim: Training on pre-1900 text only yields glimpses of post-1900 physics discoveries; a clean historical-rediscovery test is not yet achieved.
agent_test: Not testable at our scale; note as open.

claim: Relational attention is trainable by generating analogies and by making correspondences visible (Richland and McDonough high-cuing).
agent_test: Ask the agent to write explicit correspondences before transfer vs not.

claim: Near sources suit fixes and less-similar sources suit new concepts (Dunbar 1997, 2001, as summarised in the Stanford Encyclopedia), but radically different domains are rare, and the lab data are 98% within domain. The review of the later studies says goals had no effect on distance in political writing. Primary Dunbar papers were still not opened.
agent_test: Switch source distance by goal (repair vs invent) between medium and far, not near and extreme.

claim: Instruction-tuned chat models may be worse at letter-string analogy than base models (GPT-3.5 0.350 vs GPT-3 0.488).
agent_test: Compare base vs tuned on the same agent task; confounded by prompt format.

claim: Structure-first prompts help far analogies in ARN: CoT demonstrations that first extract each narrative's proverb-level message gave GPT models up to 30 points on far analogies, while plain demonstrations gave about 10 and hurt near analogies. This is not a test of a retrieval step.
agent_test: Compare message-extraction CoT vs direct comparison on far-vs-near-distractor items with a current model.

claim: A 2025 reasoning model can match humans on an abstraction benchmark but with a different rule: on ConceptARC text, o3 scores 77.1 vs humans 73.0, yet about 27% of correct o3 and Gemini answers rest on unintended or wrong rules vs about 7% for humans.
agent_test: Score the agent's stated analogy or rule, not only the answer.

claim: The claim that code makes strong models explore less rests on a correlational trace-word measure on two models (Gemini-2.5-flash drops, Qwen3-235B stable); a forced-exploration guardrail has not been tested.
agent_test: Run tool vs tool plus exploration quota at equal tokens.

claim: Human-judged novelty of LLM research ideas does not survive execution: AI novelty fell 5.778 to 4.729 while human ideas stayed 4.912 to 4.903 (43 experts, 19 human and 24 AI ideas). Planned external retrieval raises idea diversity (3.4x unique ideas, 37.5% of top-4 in a 10-expert panel) but feasibility was not scored separately.
agent_test: Judge analogy-sourced ideas by running them, not by rating the text.

claim: In a pre-1936 historical counterfactual (fluid catalytic cracking), a 7B model with the right cross-domain material in context succeeded in 2/20 trials alone and 20/20 when a human supplied the grain-silo analogy. Source selection, not mapping, was the bottleneck. No unsteered comparison with plain chain of thought exists.
agent_test: Test whether the agent can retrieve the far source itself, then compare analogy vs generic CoT.

claim: Nobody has tested a staged analogy operator (pick source, state target constraints, prune, abstract) against plain analogical prompting at equal tokens on a modern reasoning model. Nearest tests: Thought Propagation beats CoT and ToT at about ToT tokens (GPT-4 0.88 vs 0.76 and 0.46), Step-Back adds only +1.6 and +0.3 over GPT-4 CoT on MMLU Physics and Chemistry.
agent_test: Design the equal-token comparison ourselves; 3 arms: plain CoT, analogical prompting, staged operator.

claim: No independent replication or historian's critique of the Maxwell or Kepler cognitive-historical readings was found. A precedent exists for a different reconstruction (Hanson on Kepler, judged historically inadequate by Lugg 1985). Search was limited by quota.
agent_test: Not testable by the agent; treat the Maxwell staging as one author's reading.

claim: Story analogy accuracy falls with story length and scale stops helping: AnaloBench 1 / 10 / 30 sentences, GPT-4 89.1 / 66.5 / 60.7, humans 96.0 / 72.5 / 73.3; retrieving the analogous story from a bank of 200 is near random for GPT-4-Turbo and Claude.
agent_test: Add a summarise-to-relational-skeleton step before comparing long cases.

claim: Reasoning models do much better than Llama on abstract nonword relational analogies (gpt-oss 83% vs Llama 47-55%), but no reasoning model was tested on counterfactual letter strings or far story analogies in anything I could open.
agent_test: Re-run Webb and Lewis counterfactual items on the current model.
